subject: Cache retention & cross-border access - DPA redlines
messages:
From: Miguel Santos <m.santos@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — cache retention and cross-border access

Rishi,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Our legal team wanted the data residency and transient-cache language clarified in the DPA. Two specific asks from compliance:

- Allow application troubleshooting logs and transient model KV caches to be retained for up to 30 days for incident repro and audits.
- Confirm whether that transient data may be processed or routed through non-EU regions for inference/optimization (e.g., GPU pools in us-east).

Attached is our proposed language for Section 4 (Retention & Processing). Can you confirm whether Redwood can agree to 30-day transient retention and under what conditions cross-border processing would be allowed?

-Miguel
Legal Counsel, Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf (commented)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <m.santos@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — cache retention and cross-border access

Mike — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. High-level position from Redwood: we recognize troubleshooting windows are important, but we need to limit the scope of retained transient state to avoid creating persistent datasets that fall under onshore residency commitments. Proposed starting point:

- Ephemeral/troubleshooting caches retained up to 7 days by default; up to 14 days with documented justification and customer opt-in on the console.
- Any longer retention (e.g., 30 days) would require: (a) explicit customer opt-in per-tenant; (b) encryption at rest using customer-provided keys (BYOK); and (c) audit logging accessible to the customer.
- Cross-border processing: we can perform inference in non-EU regions only when (i) the customer has chosen a global routing policy or (ii) there's documented capacity fallback with prior notice. For Acme Health (regulated), we'd only route outside eu with explicit approval and contractual carve-in for onshore processing where requested.

Looping in Laura for contract language and Neha for privacy/retention compliance checks.

—Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <m.santos@acmehealth.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — draft language suggestion

Miguel, Rishi — thank you. I've drafted compromise language that balances Acme's operational needs and Redwood's residency guarantees. Key points in the attached doc:

1) "Transient operational data" defined to exclude model training data and to include only in-flight request traces, KV cache, and platform debug logs.
2) Default retention: 7 calendar days; elevated retention up to 14 calendar days permitted if Customer enables a "Retain for Troubleshooting" setting in the Console.
3) For retention beyond 14 days (e.g., 30 days), the Customer must: (i) sign a supplemental side-letter; (ii) enable BYOK for the retained artifact; and (iii) accept a cost pass-through for extended storage.
4) Cross-border access: Redwood will not route operational data outside the customer's selected region for processing unless: (a) the Customer configures a cross-region fallback in Console AND (b) Customer explicitly acknowledges temporary cross-border processing in writing.

I've highlighted redline text and added a short clause for emergency e-discovery where Redwood may export limited logs to a named third-party on receipt of a valid legal process and after notice to Customer (subject to local export controls).

I'll attach the redline summary. If this looks acceptable, we can bake it into the DPA and share for Miguel's legal review.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Redline_Summary_20270602.docx
From: Miguel Santos <m.santos@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — draft language suggestion

Laura — appreciate the practical approach. A couple of pushbacks from Acme compliance:

- 14 days still short for incident investigation teams; they prefer 30. They are open to BYOK and cost pass-through but want the default to be 30 for accounts in our vertical (healthcare).
- Regarding cross-border fallback, they want a guaranteed ability to opt into a strictly-onshore-only mode for all processing (no fallback) without impacting performance SLAs.

If we can get the side-letter route for 30 days + BYOK, Acme can accept the cross-border carve-out (i.e., no fallback unless they opt-in). Can you confirm the mechanism for side-letter and whether Redwood will accept a per-account clause that strengthens residency?

-Miguel
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <m.santos@acmehealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Final — agreed compromise and next steps

Miguel — thanks for the clarity. Per internal review, Redwood is willing to accept the side-letter approach for Acme Health to enable a 30-day transient retention window under these conditions:

- Customer executes a side-letter that amends Section 4 to set transient cache/log retention to 30 days for Acme's account.
- Side-letter requires BYOK for retained artifacts and a cost-recovery schedule (estimated incremental $X/mo based on token volume; Finance will finalize).
- Redwood will expose a console toggle "Onshore-Only Processing" that when enabled prevents cross-border fallback; this can be set at account-level and enforced by policy at the routing layer.

Next steps: Laura will produce the side-letter draft; I'll prepare a short privacy impact note for Acme's records. Please confirm whether you want Redwood to produce a redline of the main DPA plus the side-letter for signature and whether DocuSign works for execution.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
